props.title:
Indian Auto Stocks
Chassis, Braking & Body
props.sub: 24 companies · suspension · brakes · wheels · seats · glass · P/E · moat

props.name: Endurance Technologies
biz: India's largest two-wheeler component maker
Aluminium castings, suspension, braking and clutches
Operations across India and Europe

fin.note: Broad, diversified and steadily scaling across products and geographies.

props.moat: India's biggest 2W component supplier — diversified across products and Europe, and hard for OEMs to replace.

props.name: Gabriel India
biz: Shock absorbers, struts and front forks
Around 88% share of commercial-vehicle dampers
Serves every vehicle segment, plus railways

fin.note: An Anand-group restructuring widened its product base.

props.moat: A near-monopoly — roughly 88% of CV dampers — and the ride-control leader across segments.

props.name: Munjal Showa
biz: A Hero-group and Showa-of-Japan joint venture
Shock absorbers, struts and front forks
Mainly for two-wheelers

fin.note: Reliant on a few big customers like Hero and Honda.

props.moat: Solid ride-control tech via a Japanese JV — but heavily dependent on a couple of two-wheeler customers.

props.name: Jamna Auto Industries
biz: India's largest maker of leaf and parabolic springs
Suspension systems for commercial vehicles
Among the world's top spring makers

fin.note: A dominant domestic share in CV suspension springs.

props.moat: A dominant share of India's CV suspension springs — scale, OEM ties and a global top-three position.

props.name: Belrise Industries
biz: Metal chassis, body and suspension parts
For two-wheelers and four-wheelers
A large, diversified tier-1 supplier

fin.note: Newly listed in 2025; quarterly revenue runs around ₹2,400 cr.

props.moat: A big, diversified metal-parts tier-1 with scale — but relatively low margins and a fresh listing to prove out.

props.name: Steel Strips Wheels
biz: India's largest maker of steel and alloy wheel rims
Supplies every vehicle segment
Exports wheels and is growing alloy & EV rims

fin.note: Record monthly turnover in July; alloy and EV wheels are the growth.

props.moat: India's largest wheel-rim maker across every segment — scale plus a growing alloy/EV wheel mix.

props.name: Wheels India
biz: TVS-group maker of steel wheels
For cars, trucks, tractors and construction
Plus air-suspension and hydraulic parts

fin.note: Large revenue, but thin margins typical of wheels.

props.moat: A TVS-group wheel leader broadening into air-suspension — but wheels are low-margin and CV-cyclical.

props.name: Uniparts India
biz: Three-point-linkage parts and hydraulic cylinders
For off-highway farm and construction equipment
Largely for export

fin.note: High margins from a specialised global export niche.

props.moat: A global leader in three-point-linkage off-highway parts — a high-margin export niche with sticky customers.

props.name: ASK Automotive
biz: India's largest maker of 2-wheeler braking systems
Around 50% market share
Also aluminium lightweighting and EV drivetrain parts

fin.note: EV drivetrain parts open a new growth lane.

props.moat: Roughly half of India's 2-wheeler brakes — a dominant share, with EV-drivetrain optionality on top.

props.name: Sharda Motor Industries
biz: Exhaust systems and emission-control products
Catalytic converters and after-treatment
Plus suspension and roof systems

fin.note: Cheap and cash-rich — but EVs don't need exhausts.

props.moat: A strong, cheap emission-control specialist — but its core product fades if EVs win big.

props.name: Tenneco Clean Air India
biz: Part of the global Tenneco group
Exhaust, catalytic converters, after-treatment
Emission-control for auto OEMs

fin.note: Global technology, but the same EV-transition question.

props.moat: A global-tech emission-control specialist with strong OEM ties — facing the same long-term EV headwind.

props.name: Sundaram Brake Linings
biz: TVS-group maker of brake linings and pads
Clutch facings and friction materials
For CVs, cars and railways

fin.note: Barely profitable — under ₹1 crore of profit, on a very high P/E.

props.moat: A niche friction-materials maker in the TVS group — but tiny profits make the high valuation hard to justify.

props.name: Hindustan Composites
biz: Historically a friction-materials maker
Just sold its friction business to Rane (Madras)
Now largely an investment company

fin.note: Friction business sold to Rane for ₹370 cr; profit now comes mostly from investments.

props.moat: Its operating moat is gone — it has sold its friction business and is becoming an investment holding company.

props.name: Setco Automotive
biz: A leading maker of clutches for heavy trucks
Sold under the Lipe brand
Supplies OEMs and the aftermarket

fin.note: Deeply loss-making — trailing losses of about ₹163 crore.

props.moat: A leading truck-clutch brand on paper — but deep, persistent losses make it a distressed situation.

props.name: Banco Products
biz: Engine-cooling systems — radiators and oil coolers
Sealing gaskets for auto and industrial use
Europe via its NRF subsidiary

fin.note: Healthy margins and a solid European business.

props.moat: A cooling-systems specialist with a European arm (NRF) and healthy margins — a durable, unglamorous niche.

props.name: Talbros Automotive
biz: Gaskets, heat shields and chassis systems
Forgings and anti-vibration rubber parts
Through its own plants and several JVs

fin.note: A diversified small tier-1 spread across sealing and chassis.

props.moat: A diversified small tier-1 across gaskets, chassis and rubber — steady, but no single dominant product.

props.title: Body, Seats & Glass
props.sub: The parts you see and touch

props.name: Bharat Seats
biz: Complete seating systems and interiors
A Suzuki–Maruti joint venture
Works closely with the Maruti supply chain

fin.note: Captive to Maruti — steady volumes, but thin margins.

props.moat: A captive Maruti-Suzuki seating supplier — reliable volumes, but low margins and one dominant customer.

props.name: NDR Auto Components
biz: Seating systems, frames and interior trim
Carved out of the Bharat Seats/NDR group
A tier-1 interior and seating supplier

fin.note: A small, focused seating and interiors maker.

props.moat: A small seating specialist spun out of the NDR group — focused, but sub-scale next to global seat majors.

props.name: Jay Bharat Maruti
biz: Sheet-metal parts, welded assemblies and exhausts
A joint venture with Maruti Suzuki
A dedicated tier-1 to the Maruti ecosystem

fin.note: Cheap at 11× — but its fortunes track Maruti's volumes.

props.moat: A captive Maruti sheet-metal supplier — cheap and steady, but entirely tied to one customer's volumes.

props.name: Automotive Stampings
biz: Sheet-metal stampings and welded assemblies
Body-in-white and structural pressed parts
A tier-1 supplier to vehicle OEMs

fin.note: A small stamping supplier in the JBM / Tata AutoComp orbit; results are modest.

props.moat: A small structural-stampings supplier — commoditised pressed parts with little pricing power.

props.name: Munjal Auto Industries
biz: Exhaust systems, wheel rims and fuel tanks
Sheet-metal parts, mainly for two-wheelers
A Hero-group tier-1 supplier

fin.note: Slipped to a small loss last quarter; heavily reliant on Hero.

props.moat: A Hero-linked two-wheeler parts maker — but customer-concentrated and recently unprofitable.

props.name: Asahi India Glass
biz: India's largest automotive glass maker
Windshields and windows for most carmakers
Also architectural glass for buildings

fin.note: A near-monopoly in OEM auto glass, part-owned by Asahi and Maruti.

props.moat: A near-monopoly in Indian auto glass — high entry barriers, OEM lock-in, plus an architectural-glass arm.

props.name: Studds Accessories
biz: The world's largest maker of two-wheeler helmets
Sold under the Studds and SMK brands
Market leader in India, with exports

fin.note: Revenue up ~14%, but profit dipped this quarter.

props.moat: The world's largest helmet maker — a trusted safety brand, scale, and tightening helmet rules as a tailwind.

props.name: SJS Enterprises
biz: Decorative and functional aesthetic parts
Logos, dials, overlays, chrome and in-mould parts
For two-wheelers, cars and appliances

fin.note: Remarkable margins for a parts maker — design commands a premium.

props.moat: A design-led aesthetics specialist with premium margins — content-per-vehicle keeps rising as cars get fancier.

props.title: Chassis, Braking & Body — in one breath
items: Gabriel (~88% CV dampers) and Jamna own their niches
Asahi Glass & Studds: near-monopoly and world #1 helmets
Exhaust makers (Sharda, Tenneco) face the EV question
Setco is distressed; Hindustan Composites exited friction
Captive Maruti suppliers are cheap but customer-tied
Aesthetics (SJS) and cooling (Banco) are quiet high-margin niches
props.closer: Dominant share is the real moat here — and the EV shift is quietly re-drawing the map.
